newsitem.title: UK: Brady market bullish on Bulgaria after UDF victory.
newsitem.headline: Brady market bullish on Bulgaria after UDF victory.

text.p: Brady market activity was focused on Bulgaria on Monday following the weekend election victory of the "market-friendly" Union of Democratic Forces (UDF), analysts said.
"There were some strong gains on the back of the election result. We saw buying early this morning and we expect to see New York come in and buy later on," BankAmerica analyst Richard Gray said.
"Typically if you get a piece of good news that has been discounted then you ought to sell the news, but I don't see that happening this time," he said.
"Bulgaria is still remarkably cheap in spread terms and against the other Brady markets, therefore we're certainly staying long Bulgaria," Gray added.

The UDF won 52 percent of the votes. Gray said there was also the possibility of a coalition government. The first task of the new parliament and government will be to pass a 1997 budget and package of banking laws needed to implement tough measures agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
Bulgaria's interim cabinet signed a $657 million funding deal with the IMF earlier this month, which included the introduction of a restrictive monetary mechanism known as a currency board.
"There is a tremendous amount still to do," CSFB director-economics Jonathan Hoffman said."We wait and see whether the parliament can now deliver...the sooner it can get going the better."
Hoffman said Bulgaria's re-establishment of economic links with Russia was interesting. "Clearly they are opening up not just to the West, but to the former trading partners in the East as well."
Bulgaria's benchmark IAB was 1/4 up at 1100 GMT at 61-1/8 bid, over a point up from Friday's levels, traders said.
Bulgaria's FLRB were 1/4 up at 1130 GMT at 45-3/4 bid. Bulgaria's DISC were down 1/8 at 62-5/8 bid.
BankAmerica's Gray added it was interesting that the performance in the Brady market was coming from the "fringe, high-risk markets Bulgaria and Ecuador".
"It is positive for Bradies, all emerging markets and high-yielders in general," he said.
"It is a bull signal, a change of gear is coming up."
